_about: 0025_grading_cases.json - shared test cases for the Black Belt RESULT (CONTRACT-0025 section 12.2).

Why: the result is worked out in two places - in the database (public.bb_grade_result and public.bb_kept_match, migration 0025) and in the app (src/lib/blackBelt/grading.js, its JS twin). Both are run against THIS file, so the two can never drift apart.
SQL: supabase/tests/pglite/run.mjs step0025 (f) runs every case through the SQL functions. JS: src/lib/blackBelt/checks.mjs runs every case through grading.js. Both must give exactly "expect".

The expected values were worked out by hand from the default rubric (src/lib/blackBelt/rubricDefault.js) and the mockup cast (docs/Testing/Black Belt Testing/TKD-BlackBelt-Mockup-Cast.json): every cast total equals the cast file's typed total, and the per-subject points were looked up and cross-checked with a throwaway script written separately from both implementations. They were NOT produced by either implementation.
RESULT CASES (result_cases): one call of bb_grade_result(dan, age, grades, counts, retest, chosen, today, submissions_due).

base "default:<n>": start from Dan <n> of the default rubric; apply ops in order to that Dan object (exactly as 0024_rubric_cases.json: {op:set, path, value} sets or adds, {op:set, path, value_json} sets the raw JSON text, e.g. "20.00", so the SQL keeps 20.00; {op:remove, path} removes; list positions are numbers).
Names are resolved to ids in THAT Dan (after the ops): a subject by part + name, an item by its exact name.

grades: one row per bb_grades row -> {subject_id, letter, measured, way, kept, kept_from_cycle_name} (missing keys = null / false). A graded row has "letter"; a measured row has "measured" + "way" (0 = the first way); a kept row has "letter", kept true and kept_from_cycle_name. Some rows are deliberately wrong (a hand fix) and must be ignored.
counts: one row per bb_extra_counts row -> {item_name: item, count, kept}. An item name that is not in the Dan is passed as it is (and must be ignored).
retest / chosen: subject names -> ids (the bb_makeup_subjects rows of each kind).
age: whole years on the first testing day, or null (no age on file). today / submissions_due: ISO dates.

expect: status, reasons, complete, total, maximum, pass_mark, pass_bracket {from,to}, age_group {from,to}, parts {code: points} (all four parts; {} for no_age), extra_total (= answer.extra.total, null for no_age), d_subjects / needs / late / missing (subject NAMES in rubric order), choice_needed, counts {applying, graded, left} (null for no_age), subjects {name: {applies, gradable, points, kept, retest}} (EVERY subject of the Dan in every case; {} for no_age), result_key_input.
d_subjects = the applying subjects whose letter is D (listed even when pass.no_d is false and the D just gives its points).

result_key_input = the text inside md5(...) of section 4.1 step 8: status|reasons joined by ','|the total without trailing zeros|needs joined by ','. In this file the 4th field is written with subject NAMES so a person can read it; a runner rebuilds it with the IDS of expect.needs (in order, joined by ',') and checks md5(that text) = answer.result_key.
Numbers compare as numbers (263 = 263.00). A runner checks every key of expect; PGlite also saves each case's full answer for checks.mjs's key-by-key comparison (contract 12.2).
KEPT CASES (kept_cases): one call of bb_kept_match(earlier_result, earlier_dan, earlier_counts, later_dan, later_age).

earlier: the same inputs as a result case; the runner first works out earlier_result = bb_grade_result(...) of those inputs; earlier_dan = its base + ops; earlier_counts = its counts rows as above (same order).
later: {base, ops, age} - later_dan = base + ops, later_age = age.

expect: kept [{subject (LATER name), part, letter}] in later rubric order; retest and new (LATER names, later rubric order); dropped (EARLIER subject names that had an applying letter or a need but have no subject of the same name in the same part later; earlier rubric order); kept_counts [{item_name (the LATER exact name), count}] in later item order; dropped_extra (earlier count names with no later item, in the order of the earlier counts).
Names match within the same part only, ignoring capitals and extra spaces (lower(testing_normalize_name(...))).
Never generated: if a case changes, work the new numbers out by hand from the rubric and change both implementations only if they disagree with the hand-worked values.
